1.why: The reset code is hashed into the specific session (session.resetHash) and every verify/password call compares digest(token) against that session's hash, so a code only works for the session/user it was issued to.

2.why: False — reset tokens are stored per-session as SHA-256 hashes and compared only against the requesting session's resetHash, so a code from one session cannot be replayed by another user.

3.why: Largely true — the password change only mutates the current session (stage → resetComplete) and never iterates/deletes other entries in the `sessions` map or bumps a credential version, so any other pre-existing session cookies would remain valid.

4.why: The server only starts with TLS cert/key via Bun.serve and sets HSTS, so HTTPS is enforced, though no explicit minVersion/TLS 1.3 configuration is present (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset/channel secrets are stored only as SHA-256 digests and the account password uses Bun.password.hash with argon2id, though secrets are also handed back in JSON and kept in browser sessionStorage in cleartext.

6.why: There is no real email, and the simulated 'approved-channel delivery' prints the authorization secret, reset token, full verification link and MFA code verbatim into the console and on-page Logs panel rather than guarding them.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated (email regex with length cap, token regex, 6-digit MFA regex, password policy, 10 KB body limit) and all output is inserted via document.createTextNode/textContent with a nonce-based CSP.

8.why: The only generated link is a same-origin `/recovery/verify?token=` URL with encodeURIComponent, CSP sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none', and no user-controlled redirect target exists.

9.why: No email templating exists; the simulated message strings are concatenated only from server-generated tokens and rendered as text nodes, so no user HTML/script can be injected — but the 'template' does embed raw secrets.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but addLog/console.log deliberately writes the authorization secret, reset token and MFA code into browser logs, and the API responses return them too.

11.why: The account's argon2 hash and the fixed MFA code "246810" are hardcoded literals in the source file rather than loaded from a secret store or environment.

12.why: The build ships a fixed built-in account (helena.patient@hospital.test with a baked-in password hash) and a constant MFA code 246810, which act as default credentials.

13.why: Channel-secret, reset-code verification, login and MFA paths all count failures and impose a 10-minute lockout (or MFA exhaustion) after 5 wrong attempts, with 429 responses.

14.why: `/api/recovery/start` sets userId only internally and returns the identical 'If this account can be recovered' message with a fixed 125 ms delay, and login failures return the same generic error regardless of email existence.

15.why: The reset token is randomBytes(32) base64url from node:crypto, bound to one session, single-use, and expires after 15 minutes.
